candidates.name: Booking-com/multi-destination-trip-dataset
candidates.what_it_holds: The official Booking.com WSDM WebTour 2021 'Booking Challenge' dataset, published directly by Booking.com on HuggingFace (mirrors bookingchallenge.com). Train: 1,166,835 anonymized hotel reservations; test: 378,667 (total 1,545,502 rows). Columns: user_id, checkin, checkout, affiliate_id, device_class, booker_country, hotel_country, city_id, utrip_id (multi-stop trips are grouped by utrip_id, each trip's final destination concealed in test). Data window visible in samples is 2016 (Aug-Dec); the original 2021 challenge release covers roughly 2016-2017 bookings across many city_id/hotel_country codes worldwide. License CC-BY-NC-ND-4.0. Not on GitHub itself (Booking.com's GitHub orgs, 'bookingcom' and 'Booking-com', hold no data repos) but is the authoritative, directly downloadable microdata release (parquet/CSV via the `datasets` library or bookingchallenge.com).
candidates.why_useful: Real booked (not just searched/quoted) reservation-level records with checkin/checkout dates let you derive length-of-stay and multi-destination trip-chaining distributions and booker_country x hotel_country flow tables for a major competitor OTA — a genuine, non-Airbnb building block for gap #9 (competitor/adjacent supply-demand) and gap #20 (party-size/length-of-stay/cross-border proxies, via trip chains). It is a materially bigger and more structured booking-level dataset than anything currently held for Booking.com beyond the 515k reviews file.
candidates.last_activity: Dataset card last updated 6 Dec 2024 on HuggingFace

candidates.name: Booking-com/accommodation-reviews
candidates.what_it_holds: Official Booking.com-published review dataset (2023 vintage), described on its card as ~1.6M reviews across ~40,000 accommodations worldwide, filtered to 'informative' reviews (>=3 topics per the Text2Topic model), English-language. Fields: review title, positive/negative text sections, guest score, helpful votes, guest type, guest country, room nights stayed, check-in month, plus accommodation-level fields (type, overall score, country, star rating, location tags such as beach/ski/city-centre). License CC-BY-SA-4.0. Note: the HuggingFace dataset-list metadata shows only 193 rows for the 'default'/preview config, which may be a curated sample rather than the full ~1.6M set described in the card text — this discrepancy needs checking before use.
candidates.why_useful: If the full ~1.6M-review, 40k-accommodation set is actually downloadable, it is materially richer than the existing 515k Kaggle review file already held: it adds room_nights (a length-of-stay proxy), guest_type, check-in month, and property location tags (beach/ski/city-centre) that could support seasonal-mix and property-type cuts for a Booking.com comparator.
candidates.size_hint: Card describes ~1.6M reviews / 40k accommodations; HF list view shows only 193 rows for the default config (verify before use)
candidates.duplicate_of_holding: Partial duplicate/upgrade of the held 515k Booking.com Kaggle reviews dataset — flagging as a possibly larger, richer successor pending row-count verification

candidates.name: Booking-com/absa-dataset (TRABL)
candidates.what_it_holds: TRABL: aspect-based sentiment analysis dataset from Booking.com covering three travel domains (hotels, attractions, destinations). 7,566 rows total (5,768 train / 898 validation / 900 test). Each row: review_id, two annotators' label sets (aspect_term, aspect_category, opinion_span, sentiment, supporting text snippet) built from LLM-generated labels with human correction. Average review ~42 words, ~7 aspect tuples/review. License CC-BY-SA-4.0 (non-commercial research). Accepted at ACM Web Conference 2026 (WWW 2026).
candidates.why_useful: A structured, aspect-level sentiment dataset on hotel/attraction/destination reviews from a major OTA; marginal for KPI forecasting directly but could feed a text/sentiment nowcasting method (gap #14) if extended to a live pull, since it demonstrates a machine-labelable review schema.
candidates.time_coverage: Not stated; dataset published for WWW 2026

candidates.name: recsyschallenge/2019
candidates.what_it_holds: Official repo for the ACM RecSys Challenge 2019, run by trivago with TU Wien, Politecnico di Milano and Karlsruhe Institute of Technology, built on trivago's hotel search-and-click dataset (search sessions, clickouts, hotel metadata/attributes, prices as displayed in search results). Repo structure: data/ (empty placeholder — dataset itself distributed separately by trivago, not committed), docs/ (challenge/dataset documentation), src/ (baseline most-popular-item recommender, submission-format validator, scoring example). MIT license, 101 stars / 44 forks.
candidates.why_useful: Trivago is a hotel-metasearch competitor adjacent to Booking.com/Airbnb; the challenge dataset (obtained via trivago's separate distribution, not in this repo) contains real displayed-price and clickout sessions across many hotels/cities, useful as a competitor pricing/search-intent proxy if the underlying data can still be obtained; this repo is the authoritative pointer plus working baseline/scoring code.
candidates.size_hint: Repo itself is small (baseline code); underlying trivago dataset (external, not committed) historically ~900k sessions
candidates.license: MIT (code); dataset license set separately by trivago
candidates.last_activity: Repo appears stable/older (RecSys Challenge 2019); exact last-commit date not captured

candidates.name: omkarcloud/booking-scraper
candidates.what_it_holds: Open-source scraper/client targeting Booking.com search and hotel-detail pages: extracts hotel name/address/coordinates, star rating, review scores and sub-scores, live nightly/total pricing for given dates and currency, room types/bed configurations, amenities, up to 60 photos, guest reviews (25/page), Q&A, and nearby-landmark distances. No committed dataset — sample JSON response structures only. Repo shows minimal traction (1 star, 0 forks, 5 commits visible), license not clearly stated.
candidates.why_useful: A working method for pulling live Booking.com nightly prices/availability by date/market, which is the kind of realised-price signal called out in gap #2 (realised ADR/occupancy proxies) if run responsibly and periodically — but it is unrun, thin, and would need a terms-of-service decision before any pull.

candidates.name: stayapi/booking-com-review-scraper
candidates.what_it_holds: Small (2-commit) MIT-licensed client wrapping the third-party 'StayAPI' REST service to pull Booking.com guest reviews (guest name/country/traveler type, review title, positive/negative text, score, room type, nights stayed, dates, partner replies) and export to CSV/JSON (16-column flattened CSV shown in the README). Requires signing up for StayAPI (50 free test requests); not a self-contained scraper.
candidates.why_useful: Illustrates an available field schema (including 'nights stayed' per review) for Booking.com reviews, but is a thin wrapper around a paid third-party API rather than an independent data source or committed dataset.
candidates.license: MIT (wrapper code); underlying API is a commercial/paid service
candidates.last_activity: Not captured precisely; very low-traffic repo

candidates.name: BrightData/Booking.com-Listings
candidates.what_it_holds: A tiny (13-row) sample dataset published by BrightData (a commercial scraping-as-a-service vendor) demonstrating their Booking.com listings scrape output; appears to be a marketing sample rather than a usable dataset.
candidates.why_useful: Only useful as a pointer to BrightData's paid Booking.com scraping product/schema, not as data itself.

notes: Both WebSearch (session-wide quota exhausted before this scout could run any query) and github.com/search (repeatedly 429'd, apparently a shared/session-wide GitHub web-search rate limit hit by other concurrent scouts) were effectively unavailable for this run. DuckDuckGo (captcha wall), Bing (returned only GitHub's own nav pages, likely JS-rendered results not captured by WebFetch's markdown conversion), Google, Ecosia, Startpage and Marginalia were all dead ends via WebFetch for this purpose. What worked: GitHub /topics/<tag> pages (server-rendered, but most Booking.com-specific tags are literally unused -- 'booking-challenge', 'booking-com-challenge', 'booking-dataset', 'alternative-accommodation', 'hotel-dataset', 'rectour', 'recsys-challenge-2019' all show zero repos, meaning relevant repos exist but are not topic-tagged, so they are undiscoverable by topic browsing alone) and HuggingFace's dataset search/listing pages (server-rendered), which is where the two real headline finds (Booking-com's own multi-destination-trip-dataset and accommodation-reviews) live. Kaggle and Zenodo search pages are client-side rendered and returned no content via WebFetch. I could not confirm a GitHub-hosted mirror of the raw WSDM WebTour 2021 train/test CSVs (several guessed repo names -- logicai-io/wsdm2021-booking-challenge, js-aguiar/booking-challenge-2021 -- 404'd); the dataset lives on HuggingFace/bookingchallenge.com, not GitHub, as far as I could verify. Recommend a follow-up pass once `gh search` capacity frees up, specifically for 2021 WSDM Booking Challenge solution repos (many Kaggle-style teams historically publish training code + sometimes a copy of train_set.csv/test_set.csv as a repo asset), and for HuggingFace's 'booking' 40k-accommodation review file's true row count/config (the card text and the list-page row count disagree: ~1.6M vs 193).
